statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-16241 (PostgreSQL ECPG integer underflow can crash the client): an integer underflow in the ECPG client library lets a database server administrator crash an ECPG client by sending a bytea value without the mandatory prefix. PostgreSQL 16 releases before 16.15 are affected; it is fixed in 16.15: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-16241/. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/39f855e0e6b461d41680552c40e7f3a3bfd4511f, ecpg: Fix out-of-bound writes due to processing of invalid bytea data, on the REL_16_STABLE branch, tagged Security: CVE-2026-16241. We listed every file, including symbolic links, of every package built from the postgresql16 source in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, on x86_64 and aarch64, each checked against its index checksum: postgresql16, postgresql16-client, postgresql16-contrib, postgresql16-contrib-jit, postgresql16-dev, postgresql16-doc, postgresql16-jit, postgresql16-openrc, postgresql16-plperl, postgresql16-plperl-contrib, postgresql16-plpython3, postgresql16-plpython3-contrib and postgresql16-pltcl, at 16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 (Alpine 3.23 has no x86_64 build of postgresql16-plperl-contrib, postgresql16-plpython3, postgresql16-plpython3-contrib or postgresql16-pltcl at 16.14-r0). None of them contains the ECPG client libraries (libecpg, libecpg_compat, libpgtypes), in shared or static form, or the ecpg preprocessor: apart from the ecpg.1 manual page in postgresql16-doc, no file in these packages is named for ECPG or pgtypes. The static archives they do ship, libpgcommon, libpgcommon_shlib, libpgfeutils, libpgport and libpgport_shlib in postgresql16-dev, hold PostgreSQL's common, frontend-utility and portability code, not ECPG. On Alpine 3.23 the libecpg and libecpg-dev packages are built from the postgresql18 source, not from postgresql16. The vulnerable component is not present in this owner.

CVE-2026-16241 (PostgreSQL ECPG integer underflow can crash the client) is in the ECPG embedded-SQL client library: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-16241/ describes an ECPG client receiving a bytea value without the mandatory prefix, fixed in 17.11 for major version 17. This owner does not ship ECPG. Alpine builds libecpg, libpgtypes and the ecpg preprocessor only from its default PostgreSQL version, which is not postgresql17 (https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD), and every aports revision of that APKBUILD behind the published DHI postgresql17 builds leaves postgresql17 as a non-default version. We unpacked all 13 postgresql17 packages (postgresql17 and its -client, -contrib, -contrib-jit, -dev, -doc, -jit, -openrc, -plperl, -plperl-contrib, -plpython3, -plpython3-contrib and -pltcl packages; no debug packages are published) for 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0 on both x86_64 and aarch64: none contains libecpg, libpgtypes or the ecpg program in shared or static form; the only ECPG-related file is the ecpg.1 manual page in postgresql17-doc. The 5 static archives in postgresql17-dev hold only PostgreSQL's libpgcommon, libpgport and libpgfeutils objects. ECPG is provided by a separate libecpg package, which is not part of this owner.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-16241 (PostgreSQL ECPG integer underflow can crash the client) affects PostgreSQL 18 before 18.6 and is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 18.6: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-16241/ lists 18.6 as the fixed release for major version 18, and the 18.6 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/, list it. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/a14ba29b15a8b342808702e9da3e4a4532044f61 on the REL_18_STABLE branch, tagged Security: CVE-2026-16241, which is in the REL_18_6 release tag and not in REL_18_4; it changes the ECPG client library (src/interfaces/ecpg/ecpglib/data.c and error.c) so that a bytea value without the mandatory prefix is rejected with an error instead of being decoded. PostgreSQL 18.5 was never released (the 18.6 release notes say so), so although Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD, lists CVE-2026-16241 under an 18.5-r0 secfixes entry, this owner has no 18.5-r0 build and its first build that carries the fix is 18.6-r0. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built with Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD from the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version. As of 2026-11-27 the DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository publishes builds of source postgresql18 at 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64, and we checked every one of them on both architectures, with package checksums verified against the repository index. The affected code is the ECPG client library, /usr/lib/libecpg.so.6.18 in the libecpg package (and the static /usr/lib/libecpg.a in libecpg-dev), built from the same source in every one of those builds on both architectures. In each build the version strings of the postgres server binary and of the client programs (psql, pg_dump, pg_dumpall, pg_restore, pg_basebackup and pg_config) report the PostgreSQL release that matches the package version (18.1, 18.2, 18.3, 18.4, 18.6 and 18.7 respectively). The error message the fix adds, invalid input syntax for type bytea, is present in libecpg.so.6.18 and libecpg.a of 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 and absent from every earlier build, on both architectures. 18.6-r0 is the first published build carrying the fix, and 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 carry it. The earlier published builds (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0 and 18.4-r0) are built from PostgreSQL releases before 18.6 and are affected.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-16241, an integer underflow in ECPG that lets a database server administrator crash an ECPG client with a bytea value lacking the mandatory prefix, in 17.11. Within major version 17, releases before 17.11 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-16241/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.11-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6438-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-16241. The fixed version is this owner's first rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1, which packages PostgreSQL 17.11 and is no longer in the repository. Every build published now carries the fix: the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.11 in the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and in the 17.11-1 build, and PostgreSQL 17.12 in the 17.12-0 build and in the rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1, on amd64 and arm64. The earlier rebuild of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, packages PostgreSQL 17.10; it is affected and sorts below the fixed version.
